## Summary

Add the two `faucet-conformance` checks deliberately deferred from #465 — `assert_discover_roundtrips` and `assert_cancellation_flushes` — as **integration-level** checks, since neither can be made meaningful against the crate's synthetic in-memory doubles.

## Motivation

#465 added 5 of the 7 behavioral checks it proposed, and #470 adopted them across all connectors. The remaining two were skipped with a documented reason (a check that cannot fail is worthless — the crate's stated discipline), not forgotten:

- **`assert_discover_roundtrips`** — a true round-trip means taking a `DatasetDescriptor` from `Source::discover()`, deep-merging its `config_patch` into the source config, rebuilding the source, and confirming that dataset is actually readable. A synthetic double has no backing catalog to re-read from, so the round-trip half would only re-assert the double's canned output.
- **`assert_cancellation_flushes`** — asserting the #146 H16 contract (a `CancellationToken` fired mid-run stops at a page boundary and the sink flushes) requires driving the real `faucet_core::Pipeline` / `run_stream` with timing-sensitive mid-run cancellation. That is inherently flaky in a synthetic unit test and is already the domain of the pipeline-level tests in `faucet-core`.

Both are genuinely valuable at the **integration** layer (real catalog for discover; real pipeline for cancellation), which is where they belong.

## Proposed design

### `assert_discover_roundtrips` (discoverable sources only)
Signature (integration-oriented — takes a live source builder):
```rust
pub async fn assert_discover_roundtrips<S, F, Fut>(source: &S, rebuild: F)
where S: Source, F: Fn(serde_json::Value /* config_patch */) -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = Box<dyn Source>>
```
For each descriptor from `source.discover()`: deep-merge `descriptor.config_patch` onto the base config via `rebuild`, then assert the rebuilt source reads ≥0 rows without error (the dataset is selectable). Adopt in the 11 discoverable sources' testcontainers conformance tests (postgres, mysql, mssql, sqlite, mongodb, elasticsearch, bigquery, snowflake, spanner, s3, gcs), reusing each existing seeded backend.

### `assert_cancellation_flushes`
Better placed in `faucet-core`'s pipeline tests than the connector battery: build a `Pipeline` with a slow/paged source + a buffered capturing sink, fire the `CancellationToken` mid-run, and assert (a) `run_stream` returns `Ok` with a partial result and (b) the sink's `flush()` ran (buffered records are durable). This is essentially strengthening the existing #146 H16 coverage into a reusable helper; connector adoption is optional (Parquet/S3 sinks are the interesting cases).

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/conformance/src/lib.rs` (+ `doubles.rs`) — the two new `assert_*` (+ passing/`#[should_panic]` self-tests, per the crate's discipline).
- The 11 discoverable sources' `tests/conformance.rs` — invoke `assert_discover_roundtrips` in the existing live test.
- `crates/core` pipeline tests — the cancellation helper (or a conformance entry point exercised by Parquet/S3 sink tests).
- `docs/book/src/reference/conformance.md` — document the two checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Both checks exist with a passing test and a `#[should_panic]` failing test in `faucet-conformance` (or `faucet-core` for cancellation), so neither is vacuous.
- `assert_discover_roundtrips` adopted in all 11 discoverable sources.
- ≥90% patch coverage on new code.

## Out of scope
- Re-litigating the 5 checks already shipped (#465) and adopted (#470).

## References
- #465 (conformance expansion — deferred these two with rationale), #470 (adoption across all connectors).
- #211 (dataset discovery / `Source::discover`), #146 H16 (flush-completing cancellation).
- Roadmap epic #38.

32	| Registered & verified | 40 | a `verified` entry in `cli/connectors/registry.json` |
33	| Config schema | 30 | `config_schema()` returns a real, non-empty object schema |
34	| Documented | 10 | a one-line description in the connector catalog |
35	| Exactly-once delivery | 10 | source: deterministic replay from a bookmark · sink: atomic-watermark idempotent writes |
36	| Dataset discovery *(source)* | 10 | `faucet discover` introspects the catalog |
37	| Upsert / mirror *(sink)* | 6 | `write_mode: upsert \| delete` |
38	| Schema evolution *(sink)* | 4 | evolves the destination schema on drift |
39	
40	The **core contract** — a verified registry entry (40) + a real config schema
41	(30) = 70 — is the `Stable` gate. Everything else is a bonus that lifts the score
42	and adds a capability badge without gating the tier. So every conforming built-in
43	lands at `Stable`, while an incomplete third-party connector (no verified entry /
44	no schema) drops to `Experimental` / `Beta`.
45

47	
48	- **`faucet conformance`** — the full per-connector scorecard (dimension
49	  pass/fail + points, total, tier, capability badges). `--json` for CI.
50	- **`faucet list`** — a tier badge next to every compiled-in source and sink.
51	- **`cli/connectors/registry.json`** — a per-connector `tier` field, validated in
52	  CI against the computed score so the published catalog stays honest.
53	- **`faucet new connector`** — the scaffold's starting tier (⚪ Draft) plus the
54	  checklist to reach 🟢 Stable.

59	third-party `faucet-source-*` / `faucet-sink-*` crate README:

66	
67	Out-of-repo connectors are scored from their **trait-reported capabilities
68	only** — the repo-scan dimensions (verified registry entry, catalog docs) don't
69	apply, so a community connector is typically graded on its config schema and the
70	capabilities it advertises. Publish a PR adding a `verified` registry entry to

=== conformance README ===
# faucet-conformance

A reusable connector **conformance test battery** for the
[faucet-stream](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream) ecosystem. Any
`faucet-source-*` / `faucet-sink-*` crate calls it from its own `tests/` to
prove it upholds the connector contract.

**Passing this battery is the Tier-1 (supported) criterion for a connector.**
There is no separate tiering scheme — a connector is "supported" exactly when it
invokes and passes these checks in CI; connectors that don't are Tier-2
(experimental).

## Checks

| # | Function | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `assert_config_schema_valid` | ✅ implemented — `config_schema()` is a valid, round-tripping JSON Schema |
| 2 | `assert_bounded_memory` | ✅ implemented — `stream_pages` pages instead of buffering the whole set |
| 3 | `assert_bookmark_roundtrip` | ✅ implemented — a resumed run picks up *after* the emitted bookmark; strictly fewer records reappear |
| 4 | `assert_idempotent_replay` | ✅ implemented — atomic-watermark replay (or keyed-upsert) converges to one row per key, no double-writes |
| 5 | `assert_capabilities_truthful` | ✅ implemented — advertised `supports_*` capabilities match actual behavior (idempotency, schema evolution) |
| 6 | `assert_errors_not_panics` | ✅ implemented — a failing source surfaces a typed `FaucetError` without unwinding |

## Usage

```rust
use faucet_conformance as conf;

#[test]
fn config_schema_is_valid() {
    let source = MySource::new(/* … */);
    conf::assert_config_schema_valid(&source);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn streams_with_bounded_memory() {
    let source = MySource::over_n_rows(10_000);
    conf::assert_bounded_memory(&source, 500, 10_000).await;
}
```

Sinks use the value form of check 1:
`conf::assert_config_schema_valid_value(&sink.config_schema(), sink.connector_name())`.

## Doubles

`faucet_conformance::doubles` provides a `CountingSource` (lazily emits N
synthetic records in pages — genuinely bounded) and a `TestSink` (append or
keyed/upsert recording sink) for use in your own tests.

## Checks

Every check ships with both a passing and a `#[should_panic]` failing test in
this crate — a check that cannot fail is worthless.

| # | Function | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `assert_config_schema_valid` | `config_schema()` is a valid, round-tripping JSON Schema |
| 2 | `assert_bounded_memory` | `stream_pages` pages instead of buffering the whole set |
| 3 | `assert_bookmark_roundtrip` | a resumed run picks up *after* the emitted bookmark; strictly fewer records reappear |
| 4 | `assert_idempotent_replay` | atomic-watermark replay (or keyed-upsert) converges to one row per key, no double-writes |
| 5 | `assert_capabilities_truthful` | advertised `supports_*` capabilities match actual behavior (idempotency, schema evolution) |
| 6 | `assert_errors_not_panics` | a failing source surfaces a typed `FaucetError` without unwinding |
| 7 | `assert_write_modes_truthful` | a sink advertising `Upsert`/`Delete` converges by key and removes on delete; missing/null keys are reported as failed |
| 8 | `assert_schema_evolution_effective` | an evolvable sink's `evolve_schema` makes the added column appear in a fresh `current_schema()` |
| 9 | `assert_batch_size_zero_single_page` | a source built with `batch_size = 0` yields the whole result set as one page |
| 10 | `assert_connector_name_nonempty` | `connector_name()` is non-empty (an empty name becomes the `"unknown"` metric label) |
| 11 | `assert_preflight_check_wellformed` | `check()` returns `Ok(CheckReport)` with well-formed probes; a probe failure is a `Fail` probe, not an `Err` |

### Integration-level checks

These drive a **live backend** or the **real pipeline**, so they belong in a
connector's testcontainers/tempfile conformance test rather than against the
synthetic doubles:

| # | Function | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | `assert_discover_roundtrips` | every `discover()` descriptor is genuinely selectable — deep-merge its `config_patch` (via `merge_config_patch`), rebuild, and read |
| 13 | `assert_cancellation_flushes` | a mid-run cancel stops at a page boundary and flushes the sink, so buffered output survives (#146 H16) |

## The behavioral conformance battery

The score above is a **static** grade (registry entry, config schema, advertised
capabilities). It is complemented by the
[`faucet-conformance`](https://crates.io/crates/faucet-conformance) crate — a
**runtime** test battery a connector calls from its own `tests/` to prove it
actually upholds the contract, not just advertises it. There are 13 checks; each
ships with a passing *and* a `#[should_panic]` failing test in the battery, so no
check can be vacuous.

Checks 1–11 run against synthetic in-memory doubles or a single connector
instance (config-schema validity, bounded-memory paging, bookmark resume,
idempotent replay, truthful capabilities/write-modes, effective schema
evolution, `batch_size = 0` single-page, non-empty `connector_name`, well-formed
`check()` probes). Two more are **integration-level** — they need a live backend
or the real pipeline, so they live in a connector's testcontainers/tempfile
test:

- **`assert_discover_roundtrips`** *(discoverable sources)* — every dataset
  `discover()` reports is genuinely selectable: deep-merge its `config_patch`,
  rebuild the source, and read it. Adopted by all 11 catalog-backed sources
  (postgres, mysql, mssql, sqlite, mongodb, elasticsearch, bigquery, snowflake,
  spanner, s3, gcs).
- **`assert_cancellation_flushes`** — a mid-run `CancellationToken` stops at a
  page boundary and flushes the sink, so buffered output (a Parquet footer, an
  S3 multipart) survives cancellation rather than being orphaned
  ([ADR 0011](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-cooperative-cancellation.md)).

See [Authoring connectors](../extending/authoring-connectors.md#self-certify-with-the-conformance-battery)
for how to wire the battery into a new connector.

Adds the two `faucet-conformance` behavioral checks deliberately deferred from #465 — `assert_discover_roundtrips` and `assert_cancellation_flushes` — as **integration-level** checks. As #471 notes, neither can be made meaningful against the crate's synthetic in-memory doubles (a double has no backing catalog to re-read from; timing-sensitive mid-run cancellation is flaky in a unit test), so both drive a live backend / the real pipeline where they belong.

## What's added

**Check 12 — `assert_discover_roundtrips`** (discoverable sources)
For each `DatasetDescriptor` a source's `discover()` reports, deep-merge its `config_patch` onto the base config, rebuild the source, and assert the dataset is genuinely readable end-to-end (not just a name in a list). A new pure `merge_config_patch(base, patch)` helper (recursive object merge, scalar/array replace — mirroring the CLI's deep-merge) writes the `rebuild` closure in one line.

Adopted in **all 11 catalog-backed sources**: postgres, mysql, mssql, sqlite, mongodb, elasticsearch, bigquery, snowflake, spanner, s3, gcs — reusing each existing seeded backend (testcontainers / MinIO / emulator / tempfile / wiremock). GCS is `#[ignore]`d for the same reason its bounded-memory check is (the read path needs gRPC; `fake-gcs-server` is REST-only).

**Check 13 — `assert_cancellation_flushes`**
Drives the **real** `faucet_core::run_stream` with a deterministic self-cancelling source (no timers, no flakiness): one page, then the source fires the token and blocks. Asserts `run_stream` returns `Ok` with the partial result **and** the buffered sink's `flush()` ran (records are durable) — the #146 H16 / [ADR 0011](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-cooperative-cancellation.md) flush-completing cancellation contract.

Per the crate's discipline (a check that cannot fail is worthless), each new check ships with a passing **and** a `#[should_panic]` failing self-test, backed by two new doubles:
- `DiscoverableSource` (+ `empty()`) — drives the pass path and the empty-catalog / non-discoverable / unreadable-rebuild failure paths.
- `BufferedSink` (+ `broken()`) — models a sink that only commits on `flush`; the broken variant (flush drops the buffer) drives the failure path.

New lib code is at **100% patch coverage** (measured via `cargo llvm-cov`; every line of `merge_config_patch` / `assert_discover_roundtrips` / `assert_cancellation_flushes` is exercised).

content.text:
You're in good shape — this repo is unusually well-documented, and the single densest overview is already on your disk: **`CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/rules/architecture.md`**. If you read nothing else, read those two; `architecture.md` is effectively a guided tour of every crate, trait, and subsystem. Here's how I'd spend the hours before the interview.

## 1. Lock the mental model (~20 min)
- `docs/architecture/overview.md`, `docs/architecture/pipeline.md`, `docs/book/src/getting-started/concepts.md`
- `docs/engineering-principles.md` and the top of `CLAUDE.md` — the **Primary Goal** ("every connector should be the fastest way to move data between its endpoints in Rust; reliability/correctness is priority #1"). Open with this framing; it explains almost every design choice.

**One-liner to have ready:** *"faucet-stream is a config-driven, pluggable source→sink data-movement toolkit in Rust — 60+ crates, each connector depends only on `faucet-core`, driven declaratively from YAML by a `faucet` CLI, with governance (exactly-once, quality, contracts, masking, lineage) built into the pipeline rather than bolted on."*

## 2. Core architecture — the traits & the runtime (~30 min)
- `crates/core/src/traits.rs` — the `Source`/`Sink` contract. **Know why it's object-safe** (no associated types/generics on methods, all new methods defaulted): that's what makes the third-party marketplace work. This is a classic interview probe.
- `crates/core/src/pipeline.rs` — `stream_pages` + `run_stream`. This is the heart.
- ADRs are gold for "why" questions — each is short and tradeoff-framed:
  - `0001-stream-pages.md` — streaming vs buffering (bounded memory).
  - `0002-checkpoint-ordering.md` — **write → flush → persist bookmark** ordering. Memorize this; it's the crux of at-least-once correctness.
  - `0004-json-record-model.md`, `0006-state-management.md`, `0011-cooperative-cancellation.md`.

## 3. Pick 2–3 "signature" subsystems for the deep dive
Interviewers reward *depth with tradeoffs*, not breadth. Strongest stories here:

| Topic | Read | Why it's a great story |
|---|---|---|
| **Exactly-once delivery** | `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-exactly-once-delivery-design.md`, `crates/core/src/idempotency.rs` | Atomic-watermark vs keyed-upsert mechanisms; the sink-anchored resume (commit token embeds the bookmark) closing the crash window. Rich tradeoffs. |
| **Checkpoint ordering + cancellation** | ADR 0002 + ADR 0011, `run_stream` in `pipeline.rs` | Why flush must precede bookmark persist; flush-completing cooperative cancellation so a Parquet footer / S3 multipart survives. **You just worked on the conformance check for this — speak to it firsthand.** |
| **The governance pipeline** | cookbook: `dlq.md`, `quality.md`, `contracts.md`, `masking.md`, `schema-drift.md`; specs `2026-05-24-dlq-design.md`, `2026-05-29-quality-checks-design.md` | The per-page pass order (masking → quality → contract → drift → write) and *why that order*. |
| **Config → execution model** | `2026-05-18-cli-pipeline-matrix-and-dag-design.md`, `cookbook/topology.md`, `crates/core/src/topology.rs` | Matrix fan-out, parent/child DAG, topology node graph. |

## 4. Have these code files open in tabs
`crates/core/src/{traits.rs, pipeline.rs, idempotency.rs, stage.rs, error.rs}` and one representative connector end-to-end (e.g. `crates/source/rest/` — auth/pagination/extract split) so you can walk from config → stream → sink live.

## 5. Your personal angle — the conformance battery
You literally just shipped the deepest checks in it. Read `crates/conformance/src/lib.rs` and `docs/book/src/reference/conformance.md`. Great to volunteer: *"the contract isn't just prose — there's a reusable test battery (`faucet-conformance`) every connector runs in CI; passing it **is** the Tier-1 definition. Each of the 13 checks ships with a passing and a `#[should_panic]` test, because a check that can't fail is worthless."* That last line is a memorable soundbite.

## Likely questions → where the answer lives
- *"How do you guarantee no data loss on crash?"* → ADR 0002 (checkpoint ordering) + `0005-runtime-recovery.md`.
- *"How is memory bounded on a billion-row table?"* → ADR 0001, `stream_pages`, `batch_size`/`batch_size:0` semantics.
- *"How would a third party add a connector?"* → `extending/authoring-connectors.md` + object-safe traits + `faucet-core` as the only dep.
- *"Exactly-once — really?"* → idempotency spec; be honest about the *effectively-once* framing (atomic watermark + the hard gate: CDC source + idempotent sink + durable state + no DLQ).
- *"How do you back-pressure / handle a slow sink?"* → the single-page-in-flight streaming loop.
- *"How do you know a connector is correct?"* → the conformance battery (your work).

If you have limited time: **`architecture.md` → ADR 0001 & 0002 → the exactly-once spec → your conformance work.** That covers the mental model, the correctness core, the flagship feature, and a part you can speak to with genuine authority.

## Install

- `faucet` is the release name (your choice).
- `--version 1.8.1` is the latest published (also available: `1.8.0`, `1.7.1`). With Helm 3.17 you *can* omit `--version` and it resolves the highest SemVer, but pinning it is the safer habit.

A dry run first, if you want to see the manifests without touching a cluster:

```bash
helm template faucet oci://ghcr.io/faucet-hq/charts/faucet-stream --version 1.8.1
```

## Uninstall

(You said "uninstall … to install it" — I'm reading that as the uninstall command.)

```bash
helm uninstall faucet          # add -n <namespace> if you installed into one
```

Yes — you can skip it. With Helm 3.17, omitting `--version` on an OCI chart makes Helm query the registry tags and resolve the **highest SemVer**, which is `1.8.1` (confirmed above: `Pulled: …faucet-stream:1.8.1`).

```bash
helm install faucet oci://ghcr.io/faucet-hq/charts/faucet-stream
```

Two caveats worth knowing:
- **It's "latest at install time," not a floating tag.** Helm records the concrete resolved version (1.8.1) in the release. A later `helm upgrade` without `--version` re-resolves to whatever the newest published tag is then. For reproducible installs (CI, prod), pin `--version 1.8.1`; for a quick try, skipping it is fine.
- **"Highest SemVer" ignores pre-releases** (e.g. an `-rc1` tag wouldn't be picked unless you ask for it) — not relevant here since all three tags are stable releases.
